server.name: org.linkedparticles/particles
server.description: An append-only ledger of sourced, dated, confidence-scored claims your agent cites and you audit
server.title: Particles

runtimeArguments.description: The distribution that provides the server. Its console script is named `particles`, so the executable and the package name differ and `--from` is required.
runtimeArguments.name: --from

runtimeArguments.description: The console script installed by the linkedparticles distribution.

packageArguments.description: The CLI command group that hosts the Model Context Protocol surface.
Serve the belief store over stdio. Read-only by default: the read tools are always registered, and the write tools are added only for stores explicitly listed in `mcp.write.enabled_stores`.

environmentVariables.description: Anthropic API key. Required for the tools that call a model — `query` composes a cited natural-language answer, and the semantic half of `lint` reasons over claim pairs. The accessors that only read the store (`particle_show`, `particles_list`, `subjects_*`, `events_*`, `graph_view`, `quality_report`) work without it.
environmentVariables.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: SQLAlchemy URL of the belief store to serve, used as given, so write a SQLite path absolute: a relative one opens against the directory the server starts in. Without it, and without PARTICLES_CONFIG, the server serves the store `~/.particles/config.yaml` names (a relative path there is read under `~/.particles/`), or `~/.particles/particles.db` when that file names none, never a store in the directory it starts in.
environmentVariables.name: DATABASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Path to the config file holding the rest of the server's settings: additional stores, model selection per purpose, and the `mcp.write.enabled_stores` allowlist that turns the write tools on. This is the supported way to give the server settings. Without it the server reads `~/.particles/config.yaml`, never a `config.yaml` in the directory it starts in. Give it as an absolute path: a relative one is refused. When you set it, also set `DATABASE_URL` to an absolute path or name one as `storage.database_url` in the file: a server started with a config file refuses a store path relative to its working directory, and refuses to start while any store under `storage.stores` has one.
environmentVariables.name: PARTICLES_CONFIG

toolSurface.writeGate: mcp.write.enabled_stores is empty by default; a store must be named there before any write tool is registered.
